@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9080'
+title: 'Scripted stub: a gate or hold step in a child pass must not block the root pass (model lock held across the wait)'
+---
+## What
+Reported by the ACP conformance session (foundationmodelsacp-39). Script: the child session plays `[{"text":"child working"},{"gate":"<fifo>"},{"text":"child done"}]`; the root calls `agents {"op":"start agent","name":"helper","prompt":"child go"}` and then says "done". With `acp-agent-stub` at cbc2e3d, the root stays `state_update running` for 40+ seconds after the child reaches its gate step and never reports idle. It should go idle after about 6 seconds (the call returns a pending answer after the inline settle grace, `ToolMount.defaultInlineSettleGrace` = 6 s) while the child waits at the gate. A runner cannot test a held (running) child until this works.
+
+## Suspected cause (not verified)
+`ScriptedSessionBackend.play(...)` runs a pass under a hold of the scripted model (`turn`). A `gate` step (`ScriptedGate.wait(atPath:)`, with a FIFO it calls `StubChunkGate.waitForNextChunk`, a blocking open/read) and the `hold`/`holdUntilReleased` steps wait INSIDE that hold. The root's second model call (the "done" pass) needs the same model lock, so it waits until the child's gate opens. The Multitool rule says the host must not hold the model lock over a tool call; a scripted wait is the same case.
+
+## Do
+1. Prove the cause with a deterministic unit test first (RED): two sessions on one scripted model, the child pass waits in a `holdUntilReleased` (not a FIFO), the root's next pass must run and end while the child is held. Use the existing `ScriptedSessionBackend` / `ScriptedPromptFixture` fixtures. No process, no FIFO, no sleep.
+2. Fix the cause in the scripted backend: a wait step (`gate`, `hold`, `holdUntilReleased`, `elicit`) must not keep the model lock while it waits (release the hold around the wait, take it again after, as a real tool call does). Keep the order of the steps and the cancel behavior.
+3. Check that the FIFO gate (`StubChunkGate`: blocking `open`/`read`) does not block a Swift concurrency thread: run it off the cooperative pool if it does.
+4. Unit tests only. Do not run the IntegrationTests package.
+5. Write on the card the answer for the conformance session: which script gives a running child with an idle root (the exact script), and the number of seconds.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A unit test shows the root pass ends while the child pass is held.
+- [ ] `gate` with a FIFO works the same way (unit test with a FIFO created in a temp directory, if it can be made deterministic; otherwise state why not).
+- [ ] The existing scripted-model tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd`. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    ### implement — stuck
+    Reason: the suspected cause is false for the stub, and the fix on the card breaks existing tests by design. A person must decide.
+
+    **What I proved (unit tests, commit c785a15 on wt-gate)**
+    1. The stub has no model lock. `ComposedAgent` makes `ScriptedLLMContainer(playbook: .sessions(script))` with no observer, so `playPass` takes no lock. Router puts no lock around a backend. Only the test support has one (`ScriptedPassCounter`, queued model).
+    2. `StubChunkGate` already runs its blocking `open` and `read` on its own DispatchQueue. A `sample` of the test process showed the reader thread in `open` on that queue, and the Swift pool was idle. Step 3 needs no change.
+    3. Two new unit tests in `AgentsToolTests` use a real FIFO in a temp directory (no process): the child run waits at `gate` on the FIFO, the root `respond` returns with the pending envelope, and after a byte goes into the FIFO the final message comes as mail one time. One test uses grace 0 with a manual clock. One uses a real 0.5 s settle period. Both pass. They run in under 1 s. The old hold test now shares one helper with them and still passes. Run: 45 tests (AgentsToolTests, QueuedScriptedModelTests, ScriptedStubModelTests) green.
+    4. So a child run that waits (hold or FIFO) does NOT block the root pass in the stub path. The root prompt turn ends after the settle period.
+
+    **Real cause of the report (by reading, then shown by the tests)**
+    The root does not go idle because of the documented design of `SessionStateLedger` (PromptState.swift): the session is busy while Router works, and an open background run is Router work. "A prompt that ends while Router still works sends no idle. The idle comes when the work ends." In my tests `session.awaitIdle()` stays false until the child run ends. So `state_update running` for 40+ s while the child waits at the gate is the designed result. The root prompt response (`endTurn`) does come after the settle period; only `idle` is held back. This is not a bug in the scripted stub.
+
+    **Why I did not do steps 1 and 2 (the lock fix)**
+    A wait step that leaves the model lock would invert the contract of these tests: QueuedScriptedModelTests (`startHeldPass` waits for `running == 1` while the pass is held; `aSlowSecondSessionWaits...` expects `startedWhileHeld == 1`; `twoSessionsNeverRunTwoPassesAtOnce`), CancellationTests (line about 152 waits for `running == 1`; about 292), and PromptExecutionTests (QueuedScriptedFixture users). In these tests a hold means a long generation that keeps the model. I may not weaken them. The queued double also has no effect on the stub binary, so the fix would not help the conformance session.
+
+    **Answer for the conformance session**
+    - Script (the one in the report works as written): child `[{"text":"child working"},{"gate":"<fifo>"},{"text":"child done"}]`; root starts it with `agents {"op":"start agent","name":"helper","prompt":"child go"}`.
+    - What the root does: the tool call returns the pending envelope after the inline settle grace (6 s default, `ToolMount.defaultInlineSettleGrace`). The root prompt turn then ends (stop reason `endTurn`) at about 6 s. Its `state_update` stays `running` (with the child in the `background` list) until the child run ends. A "running child with an idle root" state does not exist for a run of the agents tool under the present design. The child is running and the root is also running.
+    - Seconds: about 6 s for the prompt response; no idle before the child ends.
+    - Shorten the grace for a test: there is no env var and no CLI option. `inlineSettleGrace` is only an init parameter of `RoutedACPAgent` (and `CatalogContext`); `ComposedAgent` never sets it. A minimal way: the stub binary `Tests/acp-agent-stub/main.swift` reads `ACP_AGENT_STUB_INLINE_SETTLE_GRACE` (seconds) and passes it to the `RoutedACPAgent` init through `AcpAgentCommand.launch`/`ModelChoice.stub`. I did not add it.
+
+    **Decision needed**
+    (a) If the root should go idle while an agent run is open, that changes the ledger design and a card for it is needed (it touches `PromptState`/Router work events, and the Router rule is to discuss first). (b) If the card still wants the test double changed, tell me which of the queued tests may change; or add a new step (for example a wait that leaves the model) and keep the old steps as they are.
